HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Romantic worm's-eye from the slope below the great flat assembly rock above the river at Sabi at night. Euija sprawls on the crown of the rock, one knee up, a squat wine jar in the crook of his arm, laughing at the sky, royal orange #e08a2e catching his silk from a small brazier beside him. Gyebek stands one step below on the rock face, straight as a post, hands at his sides, face blank, waiting for an order, a ring-pommel sword at his hip. Beyond them the dark river and far hills, one bright star in the east. ONE device: the rock's diagonal edge cutting the frame from lower left to upper right. Brazier sparks as bokeh. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = euija, SECOND face = gyebek; its bottom row is the only sword design. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. KING EUIJA — Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Crown: Baekje king: a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls. On Euija the two side ornaments are King Muryeong's gold diadem ornaments exactly as the attached museum photo (ignore its backdrop): a pair of thin sheet-gold flame-and-honeysuckle sprays, each a central stem with curling leaf-flames fanning up and out, pierced openwork and hung with small round gold spangles, one pinned on each side of the black silk cap and rising well above it. Colour #e08a2e. GYEBEK — Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Colour #d9b13a. PLACE Deer Rock (정사암) — attached board /pl_deer_rock.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
